newsitem.title: USA: FTC Commissioner Varney to resign in August.
newsitem.headline: FTC Commissioner Varney to resign in August.

text.p: Federal Trade Commissioner Christine Varney said Wednesday she will resign by the end of August to start an Internet commerce unit for the Washington law firm of Hogan & Hartson.
"I have been in public service for five years," she said in a telephone interview. "It's time for me to move on."

Varney is one of two commissioners who vote with FTC Chairman Robert Pitofsky, giving him a majority on the five- member board. Her departure will deprive Pitofsky of that majority unless the White House moves quickly to fill her position.
Varney, who has spearheaded the FTC's examination of privacy issues and electronic commerce on the Internet, said the commission's involvement in those issues "is institutionalized."
Now, she said, "I want to help American business succeed" in international electronic commerce.
Her departure was first reported in The Wall Street Journal.

The term of FTC Commissioner Janet Steiger has already expired. But Steiger has remained on the FTC while awaiting Senate action on her replacement, Sheila Anthony. Because of internal Senate politics, action has been on Anthony's nomination and other agency nominations.
Varney said that in her new job she hopes to help American business work around the world on the Internet, without the need for a lot of new international law.
She said that although the movie and computer industries have emhasized the need for international protection of intellectual property, contract law may work better on the Internet.
To do that, Varney said, there must be a resolution to questions about electronic signatures and other systems that permit people to pay for Internet services.

Once those issues are resolved, she said, "content providers can charge in cost-efficient ways that move us a bit out of strict adherence to intellectual property tenets that may not be as easily applicable as contract law."
Varney said she will also advise clients in the area of antitrust issues, which is the primary focus of the FTC.
